claims.text: In FCC high-entropy alloys such as CrCoNi-based systems, toughness retention is governed by nano-twin density and the degree of short-range chemical order.
Nano-twinning is an important additional deformation mode contributing to the simultaneous strength, ductility, and toughness of CrCoNi between room and cryogenic temperatures.
Short-range chemical order governs toughness retention in CrCoNi-based FCC alloys.
Tailored heat or thermomechanical treatments can increase nano-twin density and induce favorable short-range order.
A homogenized CrCoNi-based alloy has lower nano-twin density and random chemical mixing relative to the proposed treated state.
Increasing nano-twin density and favorable short-range order through treatment will improve toughness retention relative to a homogenized baseline.
Enhanced nano-twinning and short-range order reduce dislocation pile-ups.
Enhanced nano-twinning and short-range order cause multiple kink and jog formations along dislocations.
Heterogeneous lattice strain can cause multiple dislocation kinks and jogs that underpin a strength-ductility synergy.
Multiple dislocation kinks and jogs facilitate more uniform plastic deformation.
The proposed microstructural changes alleviate stress concentrations and delay premature failure.
The treated alloy will have higher fracture toughness and ductility than the untreated homogenized baseline.
The treated alloy will show increased nano-twin density and distinct short-range-order features.
The proposed relationship should hold in FCC high-entropy alloys similar to CrCoNi from room to cryogenic temperatures.
EBSD can identify and measure nano-twins through their characteristic approximately 60-degree misorientation.
